statement: Every exception must terminate in an executable decision. An exception panel is incomplete if it only diagnoses.
classification: OPERATOR EXPERIENCE (UX) invariant — a distinct class from the engineering resolution invariants. Engineering invariants govern how the system is BUILT; UX invariants govern how it BEHAVES FOR ITS HUMAN STEWARD. Operator-formalised 2026-08-03: "they have a different purpose".

canaries.assertion: A duplicate-group exception derives a recommended canonical copy from recorded quality signals, explains why in terms of those signals, states the consequence before the act (including that both records are preserved), and pre-populates an editable rationale — so the operator confirms or overrides rather than authoring from scratch.

No prose the exception surface emits contains a navigation instruction ('Go to', 'Find', 'Locate', 'in the review queue', 'individually') — the system already holds the record and must present it rather than send the operator looking.

Exceptions are split into 'recommended-resolution-available' and 'genuine-judgment-required'; copies whose signals do not separate them yield the second rather than an arbitrary preference presented as a derivation.
No code path in the resolution chain deletes a candidate source — aliasing is an update recording duplicateOfSourceId, and the dry run asserts recordsDeleted === 0 and unrelatedRecordsAffected === 0.

occurrences.defect: The Track 2 exception surface isolated exceptions correctly and then stopped at diagnosis — the exact-duplicate card read "Decide this source individually in the review queue", sending the operator to find a record the system already held.
evidence: operator screenshot of the live Laboratory > Experiments exception board, 2026-08-03

occurrences.site: Track 2 Stage 2 exception surface — components/research/Track2ProgrammePanel.tsx ExceptionsSurface, duplicate group card
occurrences.defect: The exception card recommended 'Decide this source individually in the review queue' — a navigation instruction rather than an act — while both duplicate members were already loaded in the surface's own state and the quality signals needed to rank them were already recorded on every row.

notes: It must always contain the evidence, the recommendation, the rationale, the consequence and the action. The operator should never have to reconstruct the next step.
Operator, 2026-08-03, reviewing the live Track 2 exception surface: it isolated exceptions correctly but stopped at diagnosis, telling the operator to find the record elsewhere.

ENFORCEMENT PENDING. Recorded with no canary: the resolution-board refactor that would enforce it is being built now. Per the loop's own rule an invariant without a canary is advisory prose, and the milestone-close check will say so until the enforcement point lands.

NEW CLASS. The operator formalised UX invariants as separate from engineering resolution invariants because they serve a different purpose. They share this registry and the one COMPLETION_LIFECYCLE ladder (inv.engineering.036/037 — no second store, no second vocabulary); the class is carried in `classification`.

CONSOLIDATED 2026-08-03. A second candidate for this same rule was created independently the same day (CI-2026-08-03-EXCEPTION-TERMINATES-IN-ACT-001, without the UX- prefix) by the agent that built the duplicate resolution board. One rule with two homes is the exact inv.engineering.036/037 defect this registry exists to prevent, so the duplicate was removed and its four verified canaries and its occurrence were carried here. The UX- prefixed id is canonical because it carries the operator-formalised family naming.

OPEN: IsolationException.recommendedAction is free prose, which is what allowed a navigation instruction ("Decide this source individually in the review queue") to satisfy the type while offering no act. A typed action union would make the defect structurally impossible rather than canaried. That changes the shared exception shape every stage uses and belongs in its own deliberate act.
